# Findings synthesis (trails 404/405, ~50 Entire findings, 2026-11-15)

Why reviewers keep finding things: every finding is an instance of one of eight classes. Each fix so far closed the
instance, not the class, and most guards are DENY-lists (enumerate what is wrong) where the rule needs an ALLOW-list
(enumerate what is proven, decline the rest). A deny-list is complete only until the next grammar form: the newest
finding (273: `Partial<Config>` with a `[Symbol.iterator]` key) is the same class as the six before it.

| # | Class (semantic invariant that was broken) | Findings (change) | Class-level remedy |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Silence is not evidence: absent data was treated as 'complete/none' | declare fn = complete empty body, optional-chain computed member (268); alias Pick over checker-only source collapses (267 x6); name-only filter hides another source's prop (277); `used` empty (281) | Unknown is the default state; Complete is earned. Exhaustive `match` on node/type kinds, no wildcard arm, the default arm is `Unknown`/`Declined`. One rule in the one decision function: not proven => keep listed. |
| C2 | Lossy model asserted exactness (deny-list guard) | Omit/keyof index sig, Array shadow, scope, Partial<Dict>, readonly, Required undefined (273), Symbol.iterator key (273 new) | ALLOW-list expansion: expand only members of a closed set of simple forms (identifier or string-literal key, plain/optional/readonly known, non-generic), decline everything else. Oracle generator iterates the GRAMMAR of member/key forms, not the findings. |
| C3 | Spelling used where binding is required | JSX usage by name, builtin `Array` by spelling, shadowed tags, AtFile scope, three path predicates for ambient/React | Resolve by binding or return unknown; one `declaration_origin`; no string equality on identifiers in decisions. |
| C4 | Derived state outside the dependency model | stale watch/lazy relevance (281), call-site cache, scheduler re-ask after edit (279/282) | Everything an answer reads is recorded (`deps`) or the answer is not kept; `watch_equals_fresh` model with mutation proof per dependency kind. |
| C5 | One decision, two owners | collapse lanes (267, 4 rounds), picked keys (4 readers), `annotate` x3, `{...props}` meaning, relevance map vs ADR | One function, one sink, provenance `(source, key, how)` not counts/names; lanes feed inputs, never decide. |
| C6 | Host assumptions | cgroup v1 mount (272) | Read the system's own description (mountinfo); fall back loudly. Fixed. |
| C7 | Hand-tuned policy without a reference model | scheduler fairness/starvation (279/281) | Property test against a reference model (sort by class, arrival) with the starvation rule as the spec. |
| C8 | Contract drift: code, ADR, schema disagree; fields defined but never populated | schema 8 per-component map vs ADR `used`, dead story-args, `used` empty on corpora, 281 | ADR is the contract; a field ships only with a producer, a consumer and a corpus count that is non-zero. |

Plus a process class: stacked PRs show the same code in every child (about 40% of the raw count) and merge commits
re-expose it. Remedy: merge in order, review once, retarget children.

## Pre-push gate (every slice, before the Entire reviewer ever sees it)

1. Invariants: write the 3 to 6 invariants of the slice in the PR body in these terms: 'unknown unless proven',
   'resolved by binding', 'every read recorded', 'one owner', 'wired or not defined'.
2. Grammar sweep: list every syntactic or type form the touched code can receive (all AST node kinds, all member
   and key forms, all declaration kinds) and show each one is handled or lands in the Unknown/Declined arm, by an
   EXHAUSTIVE match (no `_ =>`) or a generated test over the grammar with the oracle (checker, TS API) as judge.
3. Mutation proof: for each guard or dependency, remove it and show a test fails. A guard no test can fail is not a guard.
4. Adversarial pass: a reviewer that did not write the code gets the pattern list C1 to C8 and the grammar list and
   must try to produce a wrong output (not read the diff for style). Fix once, at the class level.
5. Then `/code-review medium` on the explicit SHA range, then push.

instance, not the class, and most guards are DENY-lists (enumerate what is wrong) where the rule needs an ALLOW-list
(enumerate what is proven, decline the rest). A deny-list is complete only until the next grammar form: the newest
finding (273: `Partial<Config>` with a `[Symbol.iterator]` key) is the same class as the six before it.

| # | Class (semantic invariant that was broken) | Findings (change) | Class-level remedy |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Silence is not evidence: absent data was treated as 'complete/none' | declare fn = complete empty body, optional-chain computed member (268); alias Pick over checker-only source collapses (267 x6); name-only filter hides another source's prop (277); `used` empty (281) | Unknown is the default state; Complete is earned. Exhaustive `match` on node/type kinds, no wildcard arm, the default arm is `Unknown`/`Declined`. One rule in the one decision function: not proven => keep listed. |
| C2 | Lossy model asserted exactness (deny-list guard) | Omit/keyof index sig, Array shadow, scope, Partial<Dict>, readonly, Required undefined (273), Symbol.iterator key (273 new) | ALLOW-list expansion: expand only members of a closed set of simple forms (identifier or string-literal key, plain/optional/readonly known, non-generic), decline everything else. Oracle generator iterates the GRAMMAR of member/key forms, not the findings. |
| C3 | Spelling used where binding is required | JSX usage by name, builtin `Array` by spelling, shadowed tags, AtFile scope, three path predicates for ambient/React | Resolve by binding or return unknown; one `declaration_origin`; no string equality on identifiers in decisions. |
| C4 | Derived state outside the dependency model | stale watch/lazy relevance (281), call-site cache, scheduler re-ask after edit (279/282) | Everything an answer reads is recorded (`deps`) or the answer is not kept; `watch_equals_fresh` model with mutation proof per dependency kind. |
| C5 | One decision, two owners | collapse lanes (267, 4 rounds), picked keys (4 readers), `annotate` x3, `{...props}` meaning, relevance map vs ADR | One function, one sink, provenance `(source, key, how)` not counts/names; lanes feed inputs, never decide. |
| C6 | Host assumptions | cgroup v1 mount (272) | Read the system's own description (mountinfo); fall back loudly. Fixed. |
| C7 | Hand-tuned policy without a reference model | scheduler fairness/starvation (279/281) | Property test against a reference model (sort by class, arrival) with the starvation rule as the spec. |
| C8 | Contract drift: code, ADR, schema disagree; fields defined but never populated | schema 8 per-component map vs ADR `used`, dead story-args, `used` empty on corpora, 281 | ADR is the contract; a field ships only with a producer, a consumer and a corpus count that is non-zero. |

Plus a process class: stacked PRs show the same code in every child (about 40% of the raw count) and merge commits
re-expose it. Remedy: merge in order, review once, retarget children.

## Pre-push gate (every slice, before the Entire reviewer ever sees it)

1. Invariants: write the 3 to 6 invariants of the slice in the PR body in these terms: 'unknown unless proven',
   'resolved by binding', 'every read recorded', 'one owner', 'wired or not defined'.
2. Grammar sweep: list every syntactic or type form the touched code can receive (all AST node kinds, all member
   and key forms, all declaration kinds) and show each one is handled or lands in the Unknown/Declined arm, by an
   EXHAUSTIVE match (no `_ =>`) or a generated test over the grammar with the oracle (checker, TS API) as judge.
3. Mutation proof: for each guard or dependency, remove it and show a test fails. A guard no test can fail is not a guard.
4. Adversarial pass: a reviewer that did not write the code gets the pattern list C1 to C8 and the grammar list and
   must try to produce a wrong output (not read the diff for style). Fix once, at the class level.
5. Then `/code-review medium` on the explicit SHA range, then push.
